SYNTHETIC FIXTURE — authored for this project's tests

# Meridian Climate Assessment, Cycle 3 (MCA-3): The Aurelian Basin

Every place, person, institution, number and finding in this document is
invented for this repository's tests. It imitates the *structure* of an
assessment report — nested headings, calibrated language — and nothing else.

## 1. Observed changes

### 1.1 Surface temperature

Mean surface temperature in the Aurelian Basin has risen by 1.9 °C between
the 1861–1880 baseline and the 2005–2024 reference period. It is *virtually
certain* that the basin's lowlands warmed faster than its coastal shelf.
Continued warming of at least a further 0.4 °C by mid-century is considered
*very likely* under every emissions pathway assessed.

### 1.2 Rainfall and drought

Annual rainfall over the southern terraces declined by 14 % over the
assessment period (*high confidence*). It is **not likely** that this decline
can be explained by internal variability alone; attribution studies place the
dominant contribution with anthropogenic forcing (*medium confidence*).

#### 1.2.1 The Verlan aquifer

Recharge of the Verlan aquifer is now below extraction in seven of ten
modelled years (*high confidence*). Recovery within a human lifetime is
judged *unlikely* if extraction continues at current rates.

## 2. Projected impacts

### 2.1 Heat extremes

Days exceeding the basin's historical 99th-percentile temperature are
projected to triple by the 2050s (*likely*). The assessment finds *low
confidence* in projections of compound heat–drought events beyond 2070,
owing to disagreement among the four regional models.

### 2.2 Ecosystems

The copperwood forests of the eastern rim are assessed as *highly
vulnerable*: a committed dieback of 30–45 % of current range is *likely*
at 2 °C of basin-mean warming.

## 3. Knowledge gaps

Observational coverage of the high plateau remains sparse before 1950;
trends there carry *low confidence* and are flagged for the next cycle.
